



Network Working Group                                         I. Lohmann
Internet-Draft                                    Independent Researcher
Intended status: Experimental                              1 August 2026
Expires: 2 February 2027


       Scientific Claim Assurance Profile for QIK-VRT EFFECT_ACK
           draft-lohmann-qikvrt-scientific-claim-assurance-00

Abstract

   This document defines an Experimental application profile for
   carrying bounded scientific-claim assurance evidence through the
   unchanged QIK-VRT EFFECT_ACK version-1 mechanism.  The profile
   separates formal proof, empirical evidence, source attribution,
   normative declarations, interpretations, and open questions.  It
   requires content identity, provenance, explicit scope, evidence-type
   compatibility, dependency closure, conflict preservation, corpus-
   relative novelty labels, and separate effect authorization.

   The profile is fail-closed and proposal-only.  It does not define a
   universal truth or novelty oracle, does not make arbitrary natural
   language automatically formal, and does not establish physical
   causation from an event trace.  It changes no EFFECT_ACK wire member,
   state, message type, CDDL rule, protocol-hash projection, release
   predicate, or IANA registry.

Status of This Memo

   This Internet-Draft is submitted in full conformance with the
   provisions of BCP 78 and BCP 79.

1.  Introduction

   Systems that retrieve, summarize, generate, measure, simulate, or
   prove information can produce outputs with materially different
   epistemic meanings.  A kernel-checked derivation, a calibrated
   measurement, a quotation, a policy requirement, an interpretation,
   and an unresolved hypothesis are not interchangeable.  Treating them
   as one undifferentiated fact class creates unsupported claims and can
   turn a successful computation into an unauthorized external effect.






Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 2]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


   This profile supplies a bounded evidence contract for applications of
   [I-D.lohmann-qikvrt-effect-ack].  A claim remains linked to the exact
   representation, scope, provenance, dependencies, evidence type,
   conflicts, and governing policy used in its evaluation.  Claim
   evaluation is separate from repository promotion, archival deposit,
   protocol submission, and physical actuation.

   The profile supports distributed, append-only knowledge meshes.  It
   specifies safety properties for content-object merge and
   classification but does not guarantee eventual delivery, global
   repository agreement, complete coverage of human knowledge, answers
   to all questions, or factual correctness of every admitted object.

1.1.  Goals

   *  Prevent an assertion from receiving a stronger epistemic status
      than its disclosed evidence type supports.

   *  Bind every evaluated claim to content identity, scope, provenance,
      dependencies, conflicts, and policy.

   *  Preserve prior objects and explicit contradictions through
      additive extension and deterministic merge.

   *  Distinguish exact corpus-relative novelty from semantic or global
      scientific novelty.

   *  Keep automated segmentation, translation, proof search, and
      classification proposal-only until the required review and
      authorization occur.

   *  Provide a common evidence boundary for software traces,
      measurements, control systems, digital twins, and quantum-
      experiment metadata.

1.2.  Non-Goals

   *  This profile does not decide the truth of arbitrary natural-
      language statements.

   *  This profile does not establish global scientific novelty,
      priority, peer review, or consensus.

   *  This profile does not guarantee complete or semantically faithful
      natural-language-to-formal translation.

   *  This profile does not infer physical causation from chronology or
      trace equality.



Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 3]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


   *  This profile does not prove a physical quantum-to-classical
      bridge, retrocausal channel, or real QPU deployment.

   *  This profile does not define an AI conformity assessment, legal
      basis, scientific publishing policy, or actuator safety case.

2.  Conventions and Definitions

   The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT",
   "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and
   "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP
   14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all
   capitals, as shown here.

   Claim envelope  A content-addressed external evidence object
      containing one atomic statement, its epistemic class and status,
      declared scope and boundary, sources, evidence, proofs,
      dependencies, explicit negations, and novelty method.

   Claim corpus  A finite declared set of claim envelopes used for one
      evaluation.  It is not an assertion of complete world knowledge.

   Formal proof receipt  A content-addressed record binding a formal
      source, compiler or kernel identity, theorem name, result, and
      observed axiom inventory.

   Observation envelope  A content-addressed record binding source
      identity, acquisition method, calibration, provenance, timing,
      uncertainty, and applicable falsification boundary.

   Corpus-relative exact novelty  The property that an exact canonical
      statement identity is absent from one explicitly identified finite
      corpus.

   Conflict  An explicit relation asserting that two claim objects
      cannot both be used as stated within an overlapping declared
      scope.  Mere difference is not automatically a conflict.

   Disposition  A successor evidence object that records the governed
      treatment of a claim or conflict without deleting the historical
      objects.

   Causality mirror  An application view that links observations,
      transformations, hypotheses, decisions, intended effects, effect
      acknowledgements, and observed effects while keeping physical
      causal attribution separately evidenced.





Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 4]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


3.  Relationship to EFFECT_ACK Version 1

   This profile uses the unchanged version-1 record specified by
   [I-D.lohmann-qikvrt-effect-ack].  It adds no member to the closed
   35-member record, no sixth state, no message type, no media type, no
   CDDL production, no protocol-hash input, no state-selection priority,
   and no IANA allocation.  Only a valid EFFECT_ACK_DONE under the
   complete base protocol permits ordinary release.

   Claim envelopes, corpora, receipts, observation envelopes, conflict
   objects, and dispositions are external content-addressed evidence.
   They are referenced through the existing evidence_refs and
   required_evidence_refs members.  The profile policy is identified
   through the existing policy_id, policy_version, and policy_hash
   members.

   Missing, inaccessible, unauthenticated, stale, ambiguous, internally
   inconsistent, or digest-mismatched required evidence MUST prevent
   EFFECT_ACK_DONE.  This profile does not select the resulting non-
   releasing state; the base protocol and bound policy do.

   Successful claim classification, formal proof, deterministic merge,
   or archive preparation MUST NOT bypass origin authentication,
   freshness, predecessor validation, policy evaluation, owner
   authorization, or any other base-protocol requirement.

4.  Epistemic Classification

   Each claim envelope MUST contain exactly one class and the compatible
   status defined below.  A profile validator MUST reject or hold open a
   mismatched pair.

   FORMAL_PROVED / PROVED  The named theorem was accepted by the bound
      formal kernel under the disclosed formal source and assumptions.
      This class does not establish that every premise describes the
      physical world.

   EMPIRICALLY_EVIDENCED / EVIDENCED  The bounded observation is
      supported by one or more valid observation envelopes.  This class
      does not establish context-free or permanent truth.

   SOURCE_BOUND / BOUND  The claim records what an identified source
      contains.  Source attribution does not promote the originating
      statement to truth.

   NORMATIVE / DECLARED  The claim is a requirement, definition,
      objective, or value decision under the identified authority or
      policy.



Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 5]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


   INTERPRETATIVE / DECLARED  The claim is an accountable interpretation
      within its declared scope and boundary.

   OPEN / OPEN  A required proof, observation, source, definition, or
      bridge is missing.  Applications MUST NOT render OPEN as
      established fact.

   A claim in FORMAL_PROVED MUST reference at least one valid formal
   proof receipt.  A claim in EMPIRICALLY_EVIDENCED MUST reference at
   least one valid observation envelope.  A claim in SOURCE_BOUND MUST
   reference at least one attributable source.  A validator MUST NOT use
   a formal proof receipt to promote a non-formal claim's physical
   truth.

5.  Claim Envelope Requirements

   A claim envelope conforming to this profile MUST provide all of the
   following:

   *  a versioned schema identifier and an application-unique claim
      identifier;

   *  one atomic canonical statement representation and its exact
      content identity;

   *  one class and compatible status from Section 4;

   *  the scope in which the claim is evaluated and a plain-language
      boundary stating what does not follow;

   *  attributable source references, applicable evidence objects, and
      applicable formal proof receipts;

   *  all material claim dependencies and explicit negation or conflict
      relations;

   *  the novelty method and the exact finite comparison corpus
      identity;

   *  the governing profile policy identity and evaluation-tool
      identity; and

   *  an effect state that remains non-releasing until the separate
      base-protocol evaluation succeeds.

   An application MAY maintain multiple canonical statement
   representations for different languages or formal systems, but it
   MUST NOT infer semantic equivalence merely from translation,



Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 6]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


   embedding proximity, model output, or shared identifiers.  Each
   asserted equivalence requires a separately reviewable relation
   object.

   Automated speech recognition, optical character recognition,
   translation, summarization, claim segmentation, premise selection,
   and proof synthesis MUST be recorded as transformations.  Their
   outputs remain candidates until the governing policy's review
   requirements are satisfied.

6.  Deterministic Evaluation

   Given a claim envelope, finite corpus, and profile policy, a
   deterministic validator MUST perform at least the following checks:

   1.  validate schema closure and canonical encoding;

   2.  verify the class and status mapping;

   3.  verify required receipt types, source bindings, observation
       fields, and every referenced digest;

   4.  resolve every dependency to exactly one admitted object in the
       declared corpus or hold the claim open;

   5.  compare the canonical statement identity with the exact declared
       corpus and label only corpus-relative exact novelty;

   6.  detect an identifier reused for different content and preserve
       the competing objects as a conflict;

   7.  preserve explicit negation edges and retain both sides of a
       contested claim; and

   8.  produce a content-addressed evaluation report whose effect state
       is non-releasing.

   A conforming validator MAY return an application-specific equivalent
   of ADMIT_AS_CLASSIFIED, HOLD_OPEN, or CONTESTED_PRESERVE_BOTH.  An
   admission indicates only that the envelope met the declared profile
   checks for its retained class.  It MUST NOT be represented as
   universal truth, global novelty, peer review, or effect
   authorization.








Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 7]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


7.  Novelty and Literature Boundaries

   Exact content or statement absence from a declared finite corpus is
   mechanically testable.  Semantic equivalence, independent prior
   publication, and global scientific priority are different questions.
   A conforming application MUST label the first as corpus-relative
   exact novelty and MUST NOT label it global scientific novelty.

   A global novelty review requires a disclosed search strategy,
   databases and versions, query terms, languages, dates, inclusion and
   exclusion criteria, deduplication method, semantic review method,
   inaccessible-source record, reviewer identity, and residual
   uncertainty.  Even a thorough review establishes bounded search
   coverage, not logical proof that no prior work exists.

   Literature retrieval tools and language models MAY propose references
   or equivalence candidates.  A profile policy SHOULD require direct
   source verification for material novelty claims and MUST retain
   unavailable or unverified references as OPEN or SOURCE_BOUND rather
   than proven.

8.  Append-Only Mesh and Conflict Preservation

   An application claiming append-only conformance MUST represent
   corrections, retractions, supersession, and dispositions as new
   objects with attributable predecessor relations.  It MUST NOT
   silently replace an admitted historical object.

   Content-object mesh merge MUST be set union over verified object
   identities.  At that layer the merge is commutative, associative, and
   idempotent.  Applications MUST preserve two objects that reuse one
   logical identifier with different content and MUST expose that
   condition for disposition.

   Replica convergence is conditional.  An application claiming
   convergence MUST disclose the considered replicas, equal validation
   and merge policy, admissible-update rules, and eventual-delivery
   assumption.  Network availability, censorship resistance, global
   discovery, complete human knowledge, and policy agreement do not
   follow from the merge algebra.

   An answer derived from the mesh SHOULD identify the minimal evidence-
   closed subgraph used, unresolved conflicts, excluded alternatives,
   applicable scope, and every OPEN dependency.  Historical derivability
   can remain visible after new evidence arrives even when a successor
   disposition changes current recommended use.





Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 8]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


9.  Causality-Mirror Requirements

   An application presenting a causality-mirror view MUST distinguish
   direct observation, transformation, model state, hypothesis,
   decision, intended effect, authorized effect, actuator
   acknowledgement, and observed feedback.  Each edge MUST identify its
   method, responsible component or principal, time boundary, content
   identity, and known uncertainty.

   Temporal succession, trace identity, deterministic replay,
   correlation, or software agreement MUST NOT be represented as
   sufficient physical causal identification.  A physical causal claim
   MUST disclose the intervention or identification strategy, applicable
   causal assumptions, plausible alternatives, falsification criterion,
   and empirical evidence.

   An application MAY use causal-model output as INTERPRETATIVE or
   EMPIRICALLY_EVIDENCED according to its observation support.  It MUST
   NOT promote the output to a context-free physical law merely because
   the computation is formally verified.

10.  Measurement, Communications, and Control

   For a claim derived from an analogue or physical measurement chain,
   the required observation evidence SHOULD identify the measurand,
   sensor or transducer, transfer function, units, calibration state,
   sampling and quantization, clock and synchronization boundary,
   uncertainty model, missing-data treatment, transformations, and raw-
   data identity.

   For a communications claim, the evidence SHOULD identify framing,
   ordering, integrity and error detection, loss and duplication
   behavior, latency model, capacity assumptions, endpoints, and
   authentication boundary.  A formal reconstruction theorem for a
   finite message MUST NOT be represented as a measurement of a real
   channel.

   For control and digital-twin applications, the evidence SHOULD
   distinguish plant observation, model version, state estimate,
   setpoint, controller output, recommendation, authorization, actuator
   command, actuator acknowledgement, and feedback measurement.  Real
   actuation MUST remain subject to the complete effect policy and
   independent system-safety validation.








Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027                [Page 9]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


11.  Quantum and Classical Evidence Boundary

   A quantum-computing or quantum-causality claim SHOULD bind circuit or
   process representation, compiler and transformation chain, backend
   identity, calibration, shot or event data, classical preprocessing
   and postprocessing, statistical method, uncertainty, null model, and
   claim interpretation.

   A mathematical model with indefinite or nonclassical causal order
   MUST NOT by itself be represented as physical future-to-past
   signalling, a controllable retrocausal channel, or modification of a
   past event.  A physical bridge claim requires a separately reviewable
   apparatus, timing and leak model, controls, falsifiable predictions,
   error analysis, and independent replication.

   This profile provides a common provenance and classification layer
   for classical and quantum components.  It does not define quantum
   semantics, prove a quantum-to-classical limit, establish VRT
   emergence, or certify a QPU implementation.

12.  Conformance and Test Cases

   A profile conformance suite SHOULD include positive and negative
   cases for all classification and dependency rules.  At minimum it
   SHOULD test a valid bound Lean receipt; a claimed proof with a
   missing or mismatched receipt; a calibrated observation envelope; an
   empirical claim without uncertainty; a source quotation represented
   as verified truth; an OPEN claim rendered as fact; an unresolved
   dependency; exact corpus-relative novelty; a global-novelty
   overclaim; an identifier collision; an explicit contradiction;
   deterministic merge under reversed input order; and an attempted
   automatic effect promotion.

   Every malformed or evidentially incomplete required object MUST
   prevent ordinary release.  A profile-valid object proceeds to the
   complete base-protocol evaluation and MUST NOT force EFFECT_ACK_DONE.

   Passing a conformance suite establishes only the tested
   implementation, revision, fixtures, and execution environment.  It is
   not proof of scientific truth, complete discovery, legal compliance,
   physical safety, interoperability with an independent implementation,
   or IETF consensus.









Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027               [Page 10]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


13.  Security Considerations

   Principal threats include forged proof or observation receipts,
   digest substitution, dependency confusion, identifier collision,
   evidence omission, source laundering, status inflation, conflict
   suppression, policy downgrade, stale evaluation replay, adversarial
   claim segmentation, malicious formal input, resource exhaustion,
   selective mesh delivery, unauthorized archive publication, and bypass
   of the effect gate.  The robustness guidance in [RFC9413] is an
   informative input to protocol and parser design.

   Implementations MUST authenticate authoritative evidence origins
   according to the deployment threat model, verify referenced digests
   and canonical encodings, bind policy and corpus identities, enforce
   freshness, preserve conflicts, and keep proposal execution isolated
   from effect executors.  They MUST bound claim size, dependency depth,
   graph traversal, proof-check time, archive retrieval, language-model
   work, and merge input.

   Formal proof checking SHOULD use a small independently reviewable
   kernel and SHOULD record compiler, source, theorem, and axiom
   inventory.  Formal inputs, generated code, source documents, and
   remote evidence MUST be treated as untrusted content and MUST NOT be
   executed merely because they are referenced by a claim.

   A content digest proves equality to supplied bytes under the named
   hash computation.  It does not authenticate origin, establish truth,
   prove semantic equivalence, guarantee future availability, or prevent
   a wholly rewritten unanchored history.  Deployments needing those
   properties require authenticated origins, independent anchors,
   retention policy, and governance.

14.  Privacy Considerations

   Scientific claim provenance can expose personal identity, health,
   behavior, location, beliefs, relationships, intellectual
   contribution, unpublished research, device topology, or confidential
   plant data.  Applications MUST minimize personal data, disclose
   purpose and retention, distinguish public metadata from access-
   controlled evidence, and authorize retrieval separately from the
   existence of a digest.  The privacy-threat analysis in [RFC6973]
   provides additional informative guidance.

   A digest is not anonymization.  Guessable or low-entropy material can
   be recovered by enumeration.  Applications SHOULD use scoped
   identifiers, high-entropy object addressing, encryption and access
   control where accountability does not require public disclosure.




Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027               [Page 11]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


   Append-only history can conflict with correction, erasure,
   confidentiality, embargo, legal hold, and research-integrity duties.
   A deployment MUST define its governing policy before collection.  A
   redaction or tombstone MUST remain attributable and MUST NOT claim
   that removed content is still independently verifiable.

   Automated knowledge meshes can amplify sensitive errors and inferred
   attributes.  Disputes and corrections MUST propagate as governed
   successor objects, and answer generation SHOULD avoid disclosing
   evidence beyond the requester's authorization.

15.  IANA Considerations

   This document requests no IANA actions.  It defines no media type,
   protocol number, registry, state, field, message type, or code point.

16.  Scientific and Governance Boundary

   This profile makes declared evidence classes, exact identities,
   dependencies, conflicts, finite-corpus novelty, and effect separation
   mechanically inspectable under a named policy.  It cannot establish
   that all relevant evidence was disclosed, that a source is honest,
   that a model corresponds to nature, that a policy is ethically or
   legally sufficient, or that arbitrary external statements are true.

   Repository persistence can establish commit and tree identity.  An
   archival deposit can establish the identity and availability of
   deposited bytes.  A formal kernel can establish derivability in its
   encoded model.  An Internet-Draft can expose a protocol proposal for
   review.  None of these facts alone establishes peer review, IETF
   consensus, scientific novelty, physical causation, deployment safety,
   or legal conformity.

   Applications MUST retain these boundaries in human-readable output.
   A concise answer MUST NOT remove a material uncertainty, OPEN
   dependency, conflict, or effect boundary merely for fluency.

17.  Implementation and Submission Status

   This section is to be removed before publishing as an RFC.

   This section is non-normative.









Lohmann                  Expires 2 February 2027               [Page 12]

Internet-Draft           QIK-VRT Claim Assurance             August 2026


   This revision is a draft-only individual Experimental application-
   profile candidate in the IETF stream.  A local deterministic claim
   validator, JSON schema, ten unit tests, and a finite Lean 4.19.0
   formalization with 21 checked theorems exist as repository
   candidates.  This statement does not assert independent
   interoperability, production deployment, physical validation, or
   standards status.

   This candidate has not been submitted to the IETF Datatracker and is
   not an RFC, IETF standard, working-group product, or IETF consensus.
   Repository persistence, deterministic rendering, or a future archival
   record would establish only the corresponding bounded facts.

Appendix A.  Changes in Revision -00

   *  Initial individual Experimental application-profile candidate.

   *  Defined six bounded epistemic classes and strict evidence-type
      compatibility.

   *  Defined deterministic claim evaluation, corpus-relative novelty,
      append-only merge, and conflict preservation requirements.

   *  Defined causality-mirror, measurement, control, digital-twin, and
      quantum evidence boundaries.

   *  Kept the complete EFFECT_ACK version-1 wire representation and
      release semantics unchanged.
